items.claim: Trailer 1 set for December 2023; first official trailer leaks
items.evidence: Trailer set to premiere in December 2023; a low-quality version leaked one day early on 4 December.

items.claim: Trailer 1 is ninety seconds long
items.evidence: Length: not stated on the page.

items.claim: Trailer 1 ends with the single number 2025 (release window)
items.evidence: It revealed a 2025 release window.

items.claim: In twenty-four hours it was watched 93 million times on YouTube
items.evidence: The article gives 93 million first-day views (third-most overall); it does not say 24 hours.
items.fix: On its first day, the trailer was watched 93 million times on YouTube.

items.claim: No video that was not a music video had ever done more in a single day
items.evidence: It set a record for most first-day views on a non-music YouTube video within 12 hours, with 46 million.
items.fix: In its first 12 hours it got 46 million views, the most any non-music YouTube video had ever got in that time.

items.claim: The company says trailer 2 was watched 475 million times in one day across every platform
items.evidence: 'a record 475 million views across all platforms within 24 hours' - the article attributes this to THR, not to the company.
items.fix: Trailer two was watched 475 million times across every platform within 24 hours, according to THR.

items.claim: Trailer two came out in May 2025
items.evidence: Released 6 May 2025.

items.claim: The trailer said 2025 and the game did not come out in 2025
items.evidence: Release window 2025 in trailer 1; first delay to 26 May 2026; second to 19 Nov 2026.

items.claim: May 2025: moved to 26 May 2026, with a quoted reason 'they need the time to reach the quality you expect'
items.evidence: Dates ok (first delay to 26 May 2026, announced May 2025). The page gives no reason for this delay; the 'quality' quote is not on the page.
items.fix: May, twenty twenty-five. The company moves it. New date: May twenty-sixth, twenty twenty-six.

items.claim: November 2025: moved again to 19 November 2026
items.evidence: Second delay to 19 November 2026, announced November 2025, for further polishing.

items.claim: Launch price 79.99 dollars
items.evidence: 'it was ultimately priced at $79.99' (Reuters citation).

items.claim: Reports say the game has no 60 FPS mode, even on the most powerful PlayStation
items.evidence: Rockstar confirmed 30 FPS on both consoles at launch (Aug 2026). Kotaku: Rockstar Technology Production Director Marc Chambers said the PS5 Pro is 'not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates'. Kotaku article dated 18 Nov 2026.
items.fix: Rockstar confirmed the game runs at 30 frames per second on both consoles at launch. Its technology director, Marc Chambers, said the PS5 Pro is not powerful enough to run the game at higher frame rates.

items.claim: No PC version at launch
items.evidence: 'no Windows release scheduled as of October 2026'; industry sources reported a PC date of Q1 2027.

items.claim: Analysts guess the new game cost between one and two billion dollars
items.evidence: 'Rumours and analysts' suggested a budget above US$1-2 billion; no specific estimator is named; Rockstar denied rumours of over US$1.5 billion but gave no figure.
items.fix: Rumours and analysts have put the cost above one to two billion dollars. Rockstar has never confirmed a figure.

items.claim: Ninety video clips of the game appear on a fan forum
items.evidence: 90 videos, showing 50 minutes of footage, published to GTAForums.

items.claim: Nobody was supposed to see them for years
items.evidence: Not stated on the page.
items.fix: Ninety video clips of the secret, unfinished game appear on a fan forum.

items.claim: The leak was on 18 September 2022
items.evidence: Date: 18 September 2022.

items.claim: The leak day was a Sunday
items.evidence: Day of the week not stated on the page.

items.claim: Staff chat message from the thief: talk to me within 24 hours or I release the code
items.evidence: The article says the hacker threatened to release the source code in a Slack message to all Rockstar staff. The 24-hour deadline is not stated.
items.fix: Inside the company, a message goes out to all staff from the thief. He threatens to release the game's source code.

items.claim: A teenager from England, part of hacker group Lapsus
items.evidence: GTA VI article: 17-year-old boy from Oxfordshire, group Lapsus$. Lapsus$ article: 16-year-old residing in Oxford, England. Ages differ between sources; England and group agree.

items.claim: He had already been arrested for hacking other giant companies; police took his laptop; he was in a hotel with no computer
items.evidence: Lapsus$ article: arrested in Oxford on 24 March 2022 (before the leak). GTA VI article: arrested 22 Sept 2022, on bail, under police protection, in a Travelodge. Hacking of other companies and laptop seizure are not stated.
items.fix: He had already been arrested earlier that year, and he was living in a hotel while on bail.

items.claim: He added a phone, a keyboard and a mouse to a streaming stick
items.evidence: Devices listed: mobile phone, television, Fire TV Stick. Keyboard and mouse are not mentioned.
items.fix: He got a streaming stick, the little thing you plug in to watch shows, and used a mobile phone.

items.claim: From that hotel TV he broke into the most expensive game in the world
items.evidence: The TV/streaming stick is supported; 'most expensive game in the world' is not stated.
items.fix: From that hotel room, he broke into the unreleased game.

items.claim: Cleanup cost five million dollars and thousands of hours of work
items.evidence: Rockstar said in court the incident cost '$5 million and thousands of staff hours to recover'.

items.claim: The court found he did it; sent to a secure hospital with no end date
items.evidence: Lapsus$ article: the indefinite hospital order ended in July 2026 and he was awaiting trial; on 16 Nov 2026 he pleaded guilty; sentencing due 23 Nov 2026. GTA VI article (older) says a jury found he committed the acts and an indefinite hospital order was made. Sources conflict on the court history; the current status is the Lapsus$ version.
items.fix: The court was told he could not stand a normal trial, so he was sent to a secure hospital with no end date. That hospital order ended in July, and this month he pleaded guilty. He is due to be sentenced on 23 November.

items.claim: The game cost more than any film ever made
items.evidence: Only rumours and analyst guesses on the budget are on the page; no film comparison is stated.

items.claim: The newest iPhone in September 2013 was the five S
items.evidence: iPhone 5s announced 10 Sept 2013, released 20 Sept 2013, unveiled with the 5c. The page does not state it was the newest on 17 Sept 2013; it was announced but not yet on sale.
items.fix: Look at the world that day. The iPhone five S had just been announced, and it would not be in shops for three more days.

items.claim: TikTok did not exist
items.evidence: No page opened covers TikTok's launch date.

items.claim: Vine had six-second videos and was shut down
items.evidence: 'record short video clips up to six seconds long'; Twitter shut down Vine on 17 January 2017 (uploads disabled Oct 2016).

items.claim: Rockstar released exactly one other big game between GTA V and GTA VI
items.evidence: Rockstar article (partial) names Red Dead Redemption 2 and also L.A. Noire: The VR Case Files (Rockstar Australia, no year). Full release list not read.

items.claim: Red Dead Redemption 2 came out in 2018
items.evidence: PS4 and Xbox One: 'October 26, 2018'; PC: 'November 5, 2019'. (The Rockstar article says 'early 2019', which conflicts with the game's own article.)

items.claim: GTA V made 800 million dollars on its first day
items.evidence: '$800 million in its first day'.

items.claim: By day three it passed one billion, the fastest entertainment product ever
items.evidence: '$1 billion in its first three days' and 'became the fastest-selling entertainment product in history'.

items.claim: It has sold more than two hundred million copies
items.evidence: 'almost 235 million copies shipped' (second-best-selling video game); the 200 million claim is consistent.

items.claim: Sold again on three generations of consoles
items.evidence: PS3/Xbox 360 17 Sept 2013; PS4/Xbox One 18 Nov 2014; PS5/Xbox Series 15 Mar 2022.

items.claim: Online city where players buy pretend money with real money
items.evidence: GTA Online exists (launched 1 Oct 2013, up to 30 players). Real-money purchase of in-game currency (Shark Cards) not found in the pages read (about 200k of 243k chars).

items.claim: Players buy the fake money every day for twelve years
items.evidence: Not stated on the pages read.

items.claim: A TV host said the game could harm society; the internet laughed
items.evidence: Host: Rachel Campos-Duffy, Fox & Friends, Sunday, days before 19 Nov; quote 'I'm not thinking this is a good thing for our culture and society'. Reaction: she was roasted online; fans called it moral panic. No studio laughter reported.
items.fix: Before this launch, a TV host said the game is not good for our culture and society. The internet roasted her for it.

items.claim: 1997, a small Scottish studio makes the first Grand Theft Auto, seen from above
items.evidence: Released Nov 1997; developed by DMA Design in Dundee (Scotland not named on the page); top-down perspective.
items.fix: Nineteen ninety-seven. A small studio in Dundee makes the first Grand Theft Auto. Tiny cars, seen from above.

items.claim: The publisher hires a famous publicist whose job is to make politicians angry and feed scary stories to newspapers
items.evidence: Campaign 'organised by publicist Max Clifford, who exploited this stirring of controversy as free promotion'. Page does not say BMG hired him or that the aim was to anger politicians.
items.fix: So a famous publicist, Max Clifford, organises the campaign. He turns the controversy into free promotion.

items.claim: The game is attacked in the British parliament before it is in the shops
items.evidence: 'discussions about banning its sale'; cited record: House of Lords, Hansard 20 May 1997, before the Nov 1997 release. 'Attacked' is not the page's wording.
items.fix: The game is debated in the House of Lords, with talk of banning its sale, months before it reaches the shops.

items.claim: The APA review says there is not enough evidence violent games cause real-world violence
items.evidence: The APA page returned empty content; wording not verified.

items.claim: GTA V released September 2013
items.evidence: Released 17 September 2013 (PS3 and Xbox 360).
